info.title: Requirements Management API
info.description: Multi-tenant API for requirements engineering, enterprise architecture, and project management. Manage software requirements, architecture principles, and architecture decision records (ADRs); model enterprise architecture (elements, relationships, views, standards) with traceability and gap/impact analysis; and run project and portfolio management (programmes, projects, resources, risks and benefits). Supports full-text and semantic search, quality scoring, WSJF/RICE prioritization, version history with snapshot comparison, and bulk operations across all entity types.

get.description:
Health check endpoint with basic diagnostics.

Carries ``tenant_refusals`` — process-lifetime counts of requests this pod
REFUSED because ``X-Tenant-Id`` named a tenant licences does not know, split
by failure class (see ``auth.tenant_resolution.record_tenant_refusal``).

⛔ IT IS HERE BECAUSE THE BURN-DOWN MUST BE READABLE FROM THE POD. This
service's Prometheus counters live on a separate metrics-only port (METRICS_PORT,
default 9921; see ``src/metrics_server.py``), which an operator on the pod does not
reach first; the alternative was a
log query, over a stream nobody retains, to answer "is anything still being
refused?". The previous answer to that question was reconstructed from the
BILLING ledger weeks after the fact.

⚠️ COUNTS ONLY — never the offending tenant values. ``/health`` is a PUBLIC
endpoint (``PUBLIC_PATHS`` in ``auth.middleware``), so anything put here
is unauthenticated. Three integers say whether the boundary is refusing
anyone; the value that was refused stays in the WARNING log, behind cluster
access, where a per-tenant question belongs.

Best-effort, like every other diagnostic in this module: if the counter
cannot be read the key is omitted rather than failing the check. ``/health``
is what a human curls when something is wrong, and it must not be the thing
that is wrong.
Kubernetes liveness probe.
Kubernetes readiness probe — database REACHABILITY, not database load.

post.description:
Create requirement with unique slug derived from title.

When ``project_id`` is set, this is a get-or-create keyed on
``(tenant_id, project_id, title)`` so an AA-intake BLOCKED→DOING re-run
updates the existing requirement in place instead of minting a duplicate.
Without this, ``EntityService._generate_unique_slug`` auto-increments the
slug (title, title-1, title-2…) and every re-run inserts a fresh row.
The gate is deliberate: a falsy ``project_id`` (non-project callers) keeps
pure create semantics. Best-effort only — an LLM-drifted title on re-run
won't match the key and will still create a new row.

get.description:
List requirements filtered by tenant_id.

``project_id`` and ``origin_kind`` are DECLARED here because they are
applied here. Both were previously sent by fr's AG-UI list actions and
dropped on the floor: FastAPI discards an undeclared query param without a
word, so the caller asked for one project and got a 200 carrying the whole
tenant — believing it was scoped. Both columns exist on ``Requirement``
(``project_id`` ``src/models/requirements.py:34``, ``origin_kind`` ``:61``),
so the filter is a real narrowing, not a rename of something else.

``origin_kind``'s domain is closed by the DB CHECK
``ck_requirements_origin_kind`` (``tenant``/``project``/``workflow``), so the
pattern mirrors ``OriginFieldsInMixin``: a value outside that set can never
match a row, and 422 is the honest answer to a knob wired to nothing.

⛔ ``card_id``, ``bound_to`` and ``visible_in`` are deliberately NOT declared
here, and this is not an oversight to "complete" later. ``bound_to`` and
``visible_in`` are **fr-local**: they are evaluated against fr's own
``asset_bindings`` table, which this service does not have and must not
guess at. ``card_id`` exists on no model in this estate at all. Declaring
any of the three here would only recreate the defect above in the other
direction — a param that parses, narrows nothing, and reads as honoured.

Filters narrow WITHIN the tenant boundary: ``EntityService.list_all`` starts
from ``scope(...)``, which applies tenant + subject visibility, and every
filter is an additional ``.where``. Nothing here can widen it.

post.description:
Create a new architecture principle.

**Project-scoped creates are get-or-create**, keyed on
``(tenant_id, origin_project_id, title)``, so an AA-intake BLOCKED→DOING
re-run updates the principle in place instead of minting a duplicate.
Without this, ``EntityService._generate_unique_slug`` auto-increments the
slug (title, title-1, title-2…) so the ``(tenant_id, slug)`` unique
constraint never fires and every re-run inserts a fresh row.

Mirrors the requirement/decision/architecture-element siblings (PRs
#63/#64), which gate their dedup on a truthy ``project_id``. ``Principle``
has no ``project_id`` column — it is tenant-wide by design ("architecture
guidance statements that apply across projects") — so the equivalent gate
here is ``origin_project_id``, which the AA-intake ``Create Principle`` node
always sets. **An un-scoped create (no ``origin_project_id``, i.e. the
general API) keeps its existing behaviour and still mints a distinct
slug** — the dedup must not change semantics for hand-authored principles
that legitimately share a title.

Best-effort, as with the siblings: an LLM-drifted title on re-run won't
match the key and will still create a new row.

get.description:
List principles filtered by tenant_id.

``origin_kind`` is declared here because it is applied here. fr's AG-UI list
action already sent it and FastAPI dropped it without a word, so the caller
got the whole tenant back with a 200 and no way to tell. The column exists
(``src/models/principles.py:51``) and its domain is closed by the DB CHECK
``ck_principles_origin_kind``, so the pattern mirrors ``OriginFieldsInMixin``
and an out-of-domain value is a 422 rather than a silent no-op.

``project_id`` filters on ``origin_project_id`` — PROVENANCE ("which
project's intake minted this principle"), NOT scoping ("the principles that
apply to this project"). ``Principle`` has no ``project_id`` column; it is
tenant-wide by design ("architecture guidance statements that apply across
projects"). A principle authored under project A that governs the whole
tenant is therefore NOT in project B's filtered list. The parameter's
published description says exactly that, so a caller is never answered with
a predicate it did not ask for (fr asked for the provenance read, 2026-10-12).
Project-scoped listing still needs the fr-side bindings (below) or a real
scoping column.

⛔ ``card_id``, ``bound_to`` and ``visible_in`` stay undeclared on purpose —
see ``routers/requirements.py::list_requirements``. ``bound_to``/
``visible_in`` are resolved against fr's own ``asset_bindings`` table, which
is not in this service; ``card_id`` exists on no model in this estate.

Filters narrow WITHIN the tenant boundary — ``EntityService.list_all`` starts
from ``scope(...)`` and every filter is an additional ``.where``.

``edge_svc`` is the GENERIC relationship service over
``architecture_relationships``, the same table that carries ArchiMate
relationships and governance links. This route used to

now, and the edge must additionally be a ``toc_nodes`` edge whose BOTH
endpoints are nodes of ``tree_id`` AND whose ``relationship_type`` is one of

``POST /architecture/relationships`` — a different route family, with its own
``DELETE /architecture/relationships/{rid}``. Without this leg the TOC path

get.description:
List direct children of an architecture element.

Bounded with the sibling's CEILING (``GET /architecture/elements``,
``le=1000``) but NOT its default: this endpoint declared no ``limit`` at all
and its query had no cap, so one fan-out parent returned the whole child set
into a ``512Mi`` / ``replicas: 1`` pod.

⚠️ ``default=1000``, deliberately NOT the sibling's ``default=100``.
The sibling is a list endpoint that has offered paging since it was written,
so its callers pass a ``limit`` and expect a page. This one is an EXISTING
UNPAGINATED endpoint acquiring a bound, and it has a real caller that sends
no query string at all and has no pagination-follow loop:
``n8n-nodes-requirements`` op ``listArchitectureElementChildren``
(``nodes/Requirements/operations/index.ts:1046``), dispatchable from AA
conveyor cards. Defaulting to 100 would silently hand that caller a truncated
child set the moment any element exceeds 100 children — trading an
availability defect for exactly the "confidently wrong answer" this PR exists
to remove. Defaulting to the ceiling keeps every caller's present behaviour
while still making the query bounded.
(Latent either way today: ``count(parent_id)`` over ``architecture_elements``
is 0 of 3,680 on production, so no element currently has any children.)

``offset`` comes with the cap on purpose — a bound with no cursor makes
every child past the first page permanently unreachable, which trades an
availability defect for a correctness one. Ordering is by ``id``, which is
uuid7 and therefore creation-ordered, so paging is stable rather than
whatever order the heap hands back. The total is reported in
``X-Total-Count`` (the house form for every list endpoint here) so a caller
can see that it has been truncated; the body stays a bare
``list[ArchitectureElementOut]``.

Return ancestor chain (nearest first), excluding the element itself.

Terminates on cyclic ``parent_id`` data (409) and on pathologically deep but
acyclic data (200 + ``X-Ancestors-Truncated``). The response body stays a
bare ``list[ArchitectureElementOut]`` in BOTH the normal and the truncated
case — the AA conveyor consumes this list positionally, so the truncation
signal goes in headers and must never become a body envelope.

post.description:
Create a new project.

When ``origin_project_id`` is set (``origin_kind='project'``: the fr project this PM
project is for) this is a get-or-create keyed on ``(tenant_id, origin_project_id)`` —
one PM project per fr project for life, closed ones included (R345, unique index
``uq_pm_projects_tenant_origin_project``). A re-POST updates that project in place
(title included) instead of minting a duplicate. When the existing row is filed under
a visibility the caller's re-POST cannot reach, it is 409 ``origin_project_exists``
(the existing id is not disclosed).

``project_type_id`` is REQUIRED (422 ``project_type_required``) and must be one of the
tenant's project types (else 422). Every project starts in its type's ``setup`` system
phase (George 10-13 v4 ruling 2 / D16): RM sets ``current_phase`` to it and writes the
first phase event (null → setup); a type without a ``setup`` phase is 409
``project_type_missing_setup_phase``. Later phase moves: ``PUT /pm/projects/{eid}/phase``.

This is the request: a fr-delegated caller may create (v4 ruling 1 / D15). Every later
write to the project is PM-only (403 ``project_writes_are_pm_only``), and that includes
a delegated ``origin_project_id`` re-POST that lands on an EXISTING row — it would update
that row in place, so it is refused with the same 403 rather than treated as a create.

A ``brief`` is REQUIRED whenever a project row is created (422 ``brief_required``): it
becomes version 1 and sets its ``constraints`` freely (immutable afterwards). On the
``origin_project_id`` re-POST that lands on an existing row the brief stays optional
(omitted = unchanged). That re-POST keeps the existing row's stored ``origin_*`` as they
are: a differing ``origin_workflow_run_id`` is ignored, never written and never a 409
(only ``PUT`` refuses an origin change). ``author_kind`` is derived from the caller
(``auth.author_kind``): ``user`` iff fr-delegated, else ``conveyor``.

403.description: ``project_writes_are_pm_only``: a fr-delegated ``origin_project_id`` re-POST that lands on an EXISTING project (a write after the request)

409.description: Conflicting change; ``brief_missing_v1`` (an ``origin_project_id`` re-POST with a brief onto an existing project that has no brief version 1); ``project_type_missing_setup_phase`` (the type does not select a ``setup`` phase); ``origin_project_exists`` (the fr project already has a PM project the caller's visibility cannot reach; its id is not disclosed)

422.description: Validation error; ``brief_required`` (a project is created without a ``brief``); ``project_type_required`` (no ``project_type_id``)

Update project.

EVERY omitted field keeps its stored value (``status``, ``created_by_user_id``, dates,
budget, ...); an explicit null clears a nullable field. ``title`` is still required.

⛔ ``origin_kind`` / ``origin_project_id`` / ``origin_workflow_run_id`` are the project's
creation identity (the POST get-or-create key): set at create, IMMUTABLE afterwards.
Omitted = kept; a value equal to the stored one is accepted (fr round-trips whole
objects); any other value, an explicit null against a stored value included, is refused
(409 ``origin_immutable``, naming the field).

An omitted ``project_type_id`` or ``wip_limit`` is unchanged; an explicit null
``wip_limit`` clears it (the catalogue policy applies again). Changing it while the project has a
current phase that the new type does not select is refused (409) — the phase is
never silently cleared; move the phase first.

A ``brief`` is appended as the next version. ⛔ Its ``constraints`` must equal the current
version's, whoever the author is (422 ``brief_constraints_immutable``): the conveyor must
never be able to loosen the gate that checks its work, and fr does not let users edit them
after create either. A project with no version 1 (a legacy row) cannot gain one here: 409
``brief_missing_v1``. ``author_kind`` is ``user`` iff fr-delegated, else ``conveyor``.

PM-only, with ONE fr exception (R345 (4)): when fr archives its project, a fr-delegated
caller may CLOSE it — body ``{"title": <any>, "status": "closed"}``. Only ``status`` is
applied: the stored title is kept (``title`` is schema-required but never written from
fr). Any other field or status from fr is 403 ``project_writes_are_pm_only``.

Set the project's current phase (n8n is the only writer; fr reads it).

Give exactly one of ``phase_id`` / ``phase`` (the phase's name). The ONLY check is
that the phase is one of the project type's selected phases (else 422 naming the
allowed phases); a project with no ``project_type_id`` is 409. Gates are approvals,
not transition rules: skipping a gated phase forward and moving backwards are both
accepted.

Idempotent: re-stamping the phase the project is already in returns 200 with
``changed: false`` and does NOT bump ``phase_updated_at`` or write a phase event.
Every real change writes one ``pm_project_phase_events`` row in the same transaction.

``restart: true`` starts a new visit even when the target is the current phase: it
bumps ``phase_updated_at`` (so the coach's per-visit caps start at zero), writes a
phase event with ``from_phase_id == to_phase_id``, and returns ``changed: true``.

``if_current_phase`` (id or name) is a compare-and-set: when present and not the
current phase, 409 with the actual ``current_phase``. An explicit ``null`` means
"expect no phase yet"; omitted means no check.

post.description:
Admit a kanban coach (R311, kanban-coach-errors.md §4.3, §4.4; PM / n8n only).

One transaction under the project row lock. A re-POST by the same ``coach_execution_id``
is answered from its row (``replayed: true``). A second coach of the same incident
(tenant, project, ``target_card_id``, ``entry``, ``root_execution_id``, ``exit_group``)
gets ``{admitted: false, reason: same_incident, winner}`` and must post nothing.
Otherwise the caps (``caps``, defaults 1/3/10) move ``requested_remedy`` only UP the order
rerun = move = repull < ask < block: a second automatic remedy in the target's entry ⇒
``ask``; an ask after an ask in the entry, or with ``ask_allowed: false`` ⇒ ``block``; the
card's cap for the current phase visit ⇒ ``block``; a NEW incident beyond the project's
cap for the current phase visit ⇒ ``block``. Every count uses the effective remedy
(``applied_remedy`` if recorded, else ``remedy``); ``note`` rows count for none. The
answer carries the counts including the admitted row.

an ``ask`` upgrade becomes ``block`` when another row of this target + entry already has
effective ``ask``; ``effective_remedy`` in the answer is what the coach applies.
